hypothesis: The DEFERRED arm of the settled-child memory lane (the TS daemon-mode whole-worker passivation - stopping the whole child WORKER process at idle, not just its kernel) needs a design analysis before any lane implements it: what the TS passivation does (what stops, what stays, the revival, the relaunch-on-prompt), what the Rust surface already has, what a Rust worker-restart-at-idle would need, and whether to implement, defer, or discard.
approach: RECORD-ONLY DESIGN LANE (no code changes). (1) The TS passivation read in full: the two-tier residency policy (core/session-action-store.ts:377-437: canPassivateSession tier-1 for parent-having children, canEvictWorker tier-2 for whole workers; idle default 90min settings-manager.ts:11), the supervisor sweep (daemon-supervisor.ts:1441-1515, cadence max(60s,min(5min,idle/3)), cap 2/worker/round, mutation-drain fence 5s), the worker-side passivateSession (daemon-mode.ts:3121-3191: single-flight per session file, the fresh-snapshot fence, releaseRlmChildSession detach then the graceful closeSession 'shutdown' - the session disposeAsync with the kernel snapshot flush, agent-session.ts:4915-5130), the passive representation (agent-roster.ts:82-106 passivatedWorkerRosterEntry; rlm-ledger.ts:903-937 the passive descendant merge), the revival paths (daemon-mode.ts:1888/2661 open joins, :3226-3349 hydratePassiveRlmSubagent chain-walk + rehydrateCompletedRlmSubagent single-flight, :3350+ the runtime replay from the session file), and the relaunch-on-prompt (daemon-supervisor.ts:3227-3282 matchWorkers->launchWorker :3467+ fresh worker process with fresh per-incarnation grants; stopWorker :6911-7010 graceful). (2) The Rust surface map: rlm_children.rs (ChildRecord, the wire calls, the watchers, the spawn/roster/collect/delete surfaces #2983 kept byte-identical), the ALREADY-EXISTING machinery (supervisor_roster.rs:249 passivate_roster_worker - the TS flipWorkerRosterEntriesInactive port running on every stop-class path; messaging.rs:192-283 wake_saved_target; rlm_roster.rs/rlm_ledger.rs passive walk; session_store.rs:578-580 header rlmDepth; #2983's stop_kernel snapshot + park arm + engine gates), and the census evidence (#2983 settle tree, worker-rss baseline, spawn-admission decompose). (3) The design doc: the durable state set, the gate set, the driver options, the stop sequence, the revival latency budget, the failure modes, the TS-parity delta table, and the recommendation.
parity_notes: NO PRODUCT CHANGE. This lane changed no repo bytes; frozen surfaces untouched by construction. The doc's parity content: the TS tier-1/tier-2 split collapses for Rust children (each child IS a worker process - the structural divergence already disclosed in #2983); the recommendation's deliberate divergences if ever implemented (armed heartbeats BLOCK the Rust stop - TS shields via hasWakeBlindSchedule; the park-arm driver instead of the supervisor sweep) are flagged for the frozen-wire review. The doc lives at /home/ubuntu/hillclimb/wave6/worker-passivation-preanalysis.md and is pushed to the bench at data/hillclimb/designs/20260928-worker-passivation-preanalysis.md.

decision: DEFER, with revisit triggers. (1) The marginal win is halved by #2983 (the kernel ~27MB/child banked) and halved again by the worker-rss redundancy lanes (the loaded shape is dominated by the B/C1/C2 derivable copies - the cheaper target already in flight); re-census after both land. (2) The 90-min idle clock rarely fires in hillclimb bench shapes (collect-within-minutes) - the win is production-shaped, not bench-shaped; a lane would ship without in-harness evidence of its own win. (3) The real work is on frozen surfaces: the passivation-aware branches (prompt follow-ups, delete, the unreachable-scorer, the wake extension to parent-owned paths) touch the roster/collect/delete semantics #2983 kept byte-identical - a lane-scale change with a byte-oracle burden. (4) Two orchestrator-owned policy decisions are unresolved: the heartbeat block vs a wake-blind port, and the idle default (TS 90min vs fleet-tuned). REVISIT TRIGGERS (any one): (a) #2983 + the worker-rss redundancy lanes merged and a fresh census still shows >=50MB/child resident at settle in production-like shapes; (b) a production-shape report of many long-idle settled children on one daemon; (c) the operator asks for the daemon idle-RSS floor below the post-#2983 baseline; (d) a TS-parity sweep of the daemon idle-eviction tier is scheduled anyway (this arm rides it: the driver + the settings port are that tier's bulk). IF IMPLEMENTED, the lane shape is scoped in the doc section 4 (the park-arm driver, the gate set with the bash probe + heartbeat block, the graceful stop via the existing stop path + passivate_roster_worker, the POSITIVE passivated status on ChildRecord, the wake extension, the roster byte-oracle + the revival oracle, and a clock-fast-forwarded same-VM A/B census). SCOPE BOUNDARY: the child worker arm only; the TS tier-2 ROOT-worker idle eviction is a separate larger port.
